title: On the density of $A+B$ when $B$ has few elements
summary: Let $\mathsf{d}$ be the asymptotic density on the positive integers $\mathbb{N}^+$. We provide sufficient conditions on an infinite set $B\subseteq \mathbb{N}^+$ so that for each $α\in [0,1]$ there exists a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}^+$ such that $\mathsf{d}(A)=0$ and $\mathsf{d}(A+B)=α$. For instance, if $(b_n: n \in \mathbb{N}^+)$ is the increasing enumeration of $B$, it is sufficient that $\liminf_n b_{n+1}/b_n>1$.
